articles.title: From tens of millions to 1,000: 140 years after vanishing, America’s bison return to the prairie
articles.description: Bison are revered as America's national mammal, symbolizing rich cultural and ecological traditions for indigenous communities. Throughout the 1800s, rampant hunting and westward expansion caused their near extinction. However, through dedicated conservation initiatives, bison populations have rebounded. Native tribes and conservation groups are now working to restore bison to their historic habitats, enriching the Great Plains and celebrating their ancestral legacy.

Woman buys old piano for $25, finds hidden Babe Ruth card that sells for $130,053 27 years later
articles.description: In 1992, Ellen Kelly bought her aunt’s old piano in Maryland for $25. While repairing a stuck pedal, a friend found 112 baseball cards hidden inside it, including a 1916 Babe Ruth rookie card. Kelly kept the discovery quiet for 27 years before selling the card at auction for $130,053, far above its estimate.

articles.title: Beetroot ice cubes for skin: A step-by-step guide to prepare and use them for a fresh-looking glow
articles.description: Somewhere between a kitchen ingredient and a genuine skincare staple, beetroot has carved out a following among people looking for a natural, budget-friendly way to perk up dull-looking skin. The idea behind this particular trend is simple, freeze beetroot juice into ice cubes and glide them over your face for a quick, refreshing boost, combining the vegetable's natural nutrients with the tightening, de-puffing effect cold temperatures have long been known to offer skin. It's genuinely easy to make at home, costs next to nothing, and takes only a few minutes of actual effort. Here's exactly how to prepare and use it properly.
